_what: Every look-ahead scenario that is not a check's Pass / Fail shape, as the fixture that makes it and the markers that must come out. THE DEFINITION, not a description of one: tools/GameHarness turns each suite into an in-game run, and tests/scenario_suites.rs puts the same scenarios to the engine over the shipped index. Adding a suite adds a test to both; neither side declares anything of its own.
_why_a_suite_and_not_a_row: A suite is what fixes a launch. The mod reads the global state file once, when it first needs it, and BepInEx reads its configuration at chainload - so scenarios that disagree about either cannot share a game, however much else they have in common. What can vary inside a suite is the save, which the probe loads in place, and the conversation, which it opens on command.
_markers: none = nothing reachable outranks the option itself, orange = it can still reach a line no save has read, red = it can still reach a line this save has not read, gaveUp = the search ran out before it could say. The mod's own rule, which both executors apply: an option that is itself unseen anywhere is never marked, since nothing outranks the top rung.
_policies: markers is one of named - the listed options must match and every other option in the menu must be unmarked - noneAnywhere, for a menu whose option ids are not known until it has been opened, and ignored, where the markers are not the subject. branches is ignored, noneAnywhere, or everyCheck with a pass and a fail half; see branch-shapes.json for what a half may hold.
_two_files: This one and branch-shapes.json, and the split is by SHAPE rather than by executor. A branch shape varies along one axis - what the two outcomes of one check land on - so its definition is a table with the conversation and entry named once and eight rows under them, and the eight-shape coverage argument is only readable in that form. Everything else varies along all of them at once, so it is written out. Both are shared definitions and both build the same in-game suite type.
_executor_specific: What only one side can run goes under a key naming the executor, offline or inGame, rather than in a scenario's own fields - a definition that reads as shared and is not is worse than two honest declarations. Two standing cases. inGame: the artefact and log checks, which read files the game wrote over a whole launch, are C# predicates, and are named here and resolved there. offline: a claim about EVERY entry in a group rather than about the options a menu happened to compose, which no in-game run can make because a menu is all it can see.
_what_is_not_here: switched-off, and only that. What it stages is a MOD SETTING - MarkLookAhead=false - and there is no such thing to stage without a mod: the offline engine has no switch to turn off, so from the same fixture it answers what the money suite answers, one option marked. A row claiming every option is unmarked would be a definition only one side could execute. It stays declared in LookAheadSuites, honestly, and the remarks there say the same.

suites.what: a crawl that runs out of budget shows nothing and says where
suites.why: The same save and the same global state as the money suite's first scenario, which marks one option - with one setting changed. That makes it a clean discriminator: if the markers still appear the budget is not being honoured, and if they vanish for any other reason the money suite would have caught it. A budget of one is exhausted before the search dequeues anything, so the best stays at seen-this-game and no option can beat its own novelty. That is the feature's deliberate failure mode - it costs a marker rather than a slow menu - and what it has to be distinguishable from is FINDING NOTHING, which is the whole point of the grey marker and of de-pvq.

LEAVING IS NOT UNCERTAIN, and that is the point rather than an oversight. The engine refuses a search it can prove cannot find anything, and that refusal builds no state, so no budget can cut it short - nothing this option reaches outranks it, which is established as firmly at a budget of one as at any other. It draws plain, which is what there is nothing down there looks like.

suites.what: an option that is itself unread anywhere is never marked, and never crawled
suites.why: The rule that gives the feature its shape: nothing outranks where such an option already leads, so a marker would say nothing. On a profile that has recorded nothing at all - a first playthrough - no option in the game is ever marked, which is a strong claim and worth holding to. And it is decided WITHOUT crawling: the engine answers from the option's own novelty and returns before it builds a state, so a first playthrough pays nothing at all for the feature. That is why the statistics artefact asserts no STATE was built rather than no crawl was asked for. The four conversations are named for their shapes rather than at random: the ceiling fan has no purchase in it, Klaasje's note is small and heavily gated, the smoker is mid-sized, and Garte is one of the largest in the game.

suites.what: the biggest conversations cost nothing when every entry is already recorded
suites.why: This suite used to be called headroom and used to be a measurement: the staged global state records every entry of every conversation, which was once the most expensive shape a crawl could take, because no option's own novelty is unseen-anywhere - so the early exit did not fire - and nothing reachable is unseen-anywhere either, so a crawl could not stop the instant it found something and had to explore everything. The no-potential-improvement short-circuit ended that: when every entry is recorded, nothing can outrank the option being asked about, so no walk can produce a marker and the crawl is skipped before any state is built. The expensive shape is now the near-opposite - a group with one unseen node, or a handful - and is measured elsewhere. What these five conversations are for now is the strongest available statement of the cheap case: they are the largest in the game, so if a crawl were going to run anywhere it would run here, and the claim is that not one does.
suites._size: The five are ranks two to six of the game's 1,501 conversations by entry count - 368, 14, 631, 28 and 1030, from 1,770 entries down to 1,476 - and tests/all_seen.rs holds them to that against the shipped index rather than taking it on trust. The largest, 362, is not among them. ENTRY COUNT IS NOT THE COST: the budget counts entry-and-state pairs, so what blows up is the state slots a conversation touches multiplied by its reachable entries, and the count turns out to be a poor proxy - 1030 is the sixth largest and its crawls peak at 201 states, a thousandth of Joyce's. It is still the only ordering available without running them.
suites.settingsWhy: Kept on so that a crawl WOULD leave a trace. The claim is that the files say nothing happened; that means nothing unless the run was configured to write them.

Conversation 656 offers exactly two things - 3, 'Move your hand, fast!', carrying DifficultyRed, and 7, '[Discard chance.]' - and neither carries a marker of its own, because a rolled check draws none (de-8hh2.2) and declining reaches nothing unread. It is the one place in the game where a RED check is the first thing offered, which is what de-8hh2.9 went looking for and why the suite exists at all. It was declared in code until it had a claim both executors could check; it has one now, so it lives here like everything else.
